clue.text: I place announcement: 'Divers rate swimming

indicators.note: letters that are swimming are moving about, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes divers' performance in a pool, as if commentating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' reworks the letters of DIVERS RATE; the definition is what such a person might say about themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who places notices or promotions in the press is the sort of person who might say that line.

clue.text: Fellow upset about programme's third host

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reversed name surrounds the next piece
in a down clue, upset turns the name upside down, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a fellow is a man, here given a man's name, Nigel

indicators.note: the third letter of the word programme is taken

explanation.surface: A man is unhappy about the presenter of the third episode of a TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NIGEL into LEGIN, and 'about' puts O, the third letter of 'programme', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a great multitude, as can this word for a vast army or crowd.

clue.text: Transport complete water supply with skill

parts.note: a full water supply has both taps, H and C, hot and cold
skill means art

explanation.surface: Bringing in plumbing for a house calls for competence.
explanation.walkthrough: Taps are marked H and C, so a complete supply is 'H and C'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cart pushed by hand is a simple means of carrying goods.

clue.text: Articles about mostly mad region

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two articles go round the next piece

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, so articles give two As

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: mad means rabid

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces on a mostly crazy part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts RABID to RABI, which sits between the two As.
explanation.definitionFit: The Middle Eastern peninsula is a large geographical area.

clue.text: Plant recipe ignored by rampant carnivore

indicators.note: rampant means running wild, so the remaining letters are rearranged
ignored by means left out of the following word

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A meat-eater on the rampage has no interest in a salad recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored by' takes R out of CARNIVORE, leaving CANIVORE, and 'rampant' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a garden flower of this genus.

clue.text: Expert containing new eruption?

indicators.note: containing means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: an expert is an ace

explanation.surface: A specialist dealing with a fresh outbreak of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the eruption is on the skin, not a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots breaking out on the skin can be called an eruption.

clue.text: Lazy student put in incomplete suggestion

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the next piece
incomplete means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a suggestion is an idea
L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A lazy student offers only half a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' trims IDEA to IDE, and 'put in' places L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone unwilling to work or doing nothing.

clue.text: Loathing bar with no cheer, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A pub without any merriment is something to detest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges BAR and NO CHEER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean intense hatred or disgust.

clue.text: Beggar's tale barely securing rotten crust, OK?

indicators.note: securing means holding the next piece within it

parts.note: barely means hardly

indicators.note: rotten means spoilt, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beggar asks whether a mouldy crust is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' turns CRUST and OK into UCKSTOR, which HARDLY holds after its L.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story told to win sympathy or money is what a beggar recites.

clue.text: Be less constrained in puzzle

parts.note: less constrained means more untamed, wilder

explanation.surface: An instruction to loosen up when working at a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To confuse or baffle someone is to perplex them.

clue.text: Telephone left in arbour

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: an arbour is a leafy shelter, a bower

explanation.surface: A phone has been left out in the garden shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is old British slang for the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang names a phone after what you speak into.

clue.text: More than half African country following initially Soviet lines

indicators.note: following puts the cut country after the Soviet letter
initially takes the opening letter of the next word
more than half keeps five of the eight letters and drops the rest

parts.note: Tanzania is a country in East Africa

explanation.surface: Most of an African nation sat behind Soviet lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than half' cuts TANZANIA to TANZA; 'following' puts it after S, the first letter of 'Soviet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A verse of a poem is a group of lines.

clue.text: Supports swallowing a French wine's dregs?

indicators.note: swallowing means taking the next pieces inside

parts.note: legs support a table or a body
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: Table legs absorb spilt French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' puts A and VIN inside LEGS.
explanation.definitionFit: What remains after the rest is used, scraps and residue.

clue.text: Senior soldier reduced to conscripting one new group of a given age

indicators.note: reduced means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a general is a high-ranking army officer

indicators.note: conscripting means taking in, so the word holds the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A general is demoted for drafting a new recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts GENERAL to GENERA; 'conscripting' puts I inside TO; then N.
explanation.definitionFit: People born and living at about the same time form a cohort.

clue.text: Theatrical device seen in version of Faust (nice and arty)

indicators.note: a version of something is a different arrangement, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A stage production of Goethe's Faust that is pretty and arty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges FAUST, NICE and ARTY; 'and' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireproof screen lowered between stage and audience is a piece of stage equipment.

clue.text: All the runners had a year to find successful patch?

parts.note: the field is everyone running in a race
had is shortened to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: The competitors spent a year looking for good ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patch' means a period, as in a good patch, not a piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A time of great success or enjoyment is a good spell.

clue.text: It's in error in German composer's record

indicators.note: the second in places the rearranged letters inside the composer's name

parts.note: Max Reger was a German composer

indicators.note: in error means wrongly placed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A mistake has crept into a German composer's archive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' turns ITS into IST, and the second 'in' puts it inside REGER (Max Reger, German composer).
explanation.definitionFit: An official list of entries is a written log.

clue.text: Fell gives our rocks

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hill in the Lake District hands over its stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a hill, a word common in northern England; here it is the old adjective meaning cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell as an adjective means fierce or deadly, as does this word for severe harm.

clue.text: Individual keeping man in position to score

indicators.note: keeping means holding the next piece within it

parts.note: an individual is one
Sid is a man's name

explanation.surface: A single player marking a man so he can score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts SID inside ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a player not offside is legally placed to receive the ball and score.

clue.text: Against being accepted by energetic person with new rule

indicators.note: being accepted by means going inside the next piece

parts.note: a goer is a lively, energetic person
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: Opposition is welcomed by a dynamic leader with fresh rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being accepted by' puts V inside GOER, and N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To control a state or people is to rule over it.

clue.text: Measure of library's capacity?

parts.note: reads as how much a library can hold; the word is both an amount of space and a book in a library

explanation.surface: A question about how much a library can hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure of space taken up, and a single book on library shelves.

clue.text: Doctor's transport is almost delayed at first

indicators.note: at first puts the shortened word before the other piece
almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: delayed means tardy, late

explanation.surface: Bus service is nearly always late at the start of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts TARDY to TARD, which comes 'at first', before IS. Doctor Who is a British TV time traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: The time machine of Doctor Who, shaped like a police box.

clue.text: Thirteen letters? It's not much

definitions.meaning: the first thirteen letters of the alphabet are the run from A to M, read as a phrase
a tiny particle, the smallest amount

explanation.surface: A thirteen-letter word is not much of a word.
explanation.walkthrough: The first thirteen letters of the alphabet run 'A to M'; the question mark flags that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabet's first stretch, and a minute particle meaning a tiny amount.

clue.text: Ancient former schoolboy only half of Eton recalled

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil
only means sole

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards
half of takes the first two of the four letters

explanation.surface: An elderly old boy remembers only part of his days at Eton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes ET from Eton (an English private school) and 'recalled' turns it to TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of date and no longer in use, as old as can be.

clue.text: He had a doctor attending his eye

definitions.text: He had a doctor attending his eye

parts.words: He had a doctor attending his eye
parts.note: reads as a patient with eye trouble; really the author whose private eye detective was always accompanied by Dr Watson

explanation.surface: A man with an eye problem saw a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye' is a private eye, the detective Sherlock Holmes, and the doctor is Watson.
explanation.definitionFit: The creator of Sherlock Holmes gave his detective a doctor companion.

clue.text: No order in revolving satellite

indicators.note: revolving means turning round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A satellite circles in no particular order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' turns NO and OM (Order of Merit) round together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earth's natural companion in space is a satellite.
